Package opsdir-adapter-elastic, entry point elastic. naming (stream names, policy/template names, languages, kibana-space setting), lifecycle (ILM/component template/SLM documents and notes), detections (ES|QL wrap, rule bodies, notes), shipping (Elastic Agent action, container blocker), api and terraform (render targets), render (orchestrator), read (importers elastic/elasticsearch and elastic/kibana), collect (two collectors).
attributes.external_dependencies: ["Elasticsearch ILM, SLM, component template and data stream APIs (GET _ilm/policy, _slm/policy, _data_stream)", "Kibana detection engine API (/api/detection_engine/rules, _find, _import NDJSON)", "elastic/elasticstack Terraform provider (~> 0.16.6)", "Elastic Stack 8.x/9.x (current 9.5.5); ECS"]
attributes.purpose: SIEM add-on: the Elastic data streams an environment keeps logs in (ILM policy attached by the dataset's @custom component template, SLM snapshot archive), its detections as ES|QL detection rules, as API documents and Terraform for elastic/elasticstack; read back from the Elasticsearch and Kibana APIs (read-only collectors, API key) and its own documents (round trip).

attributes.description: A SIEM as a log destination. A ciamLogDestination of kind siem-index keeps logs searchable (ciamRetentionDays) and in all, archive included (ciamTotalRetentionDays), the archive kept where ciamArchiveRef says; the log checks hold the total to the route's obligation and name logs kept only in the archive. A detection is an alarm binding naming the SIEM index it searches (ciamLogDestinationRole) with its search as its metric, written in ciamSearchLanguage (the SIEM adapters' vocabulary; not recorded: the SIEM's native language), rendered with the rule's count-per-window condition; cloud alarm renderers leave detections to the SIEM, and a SIEM's importers say nothing about entries other SIEMs or clouds keep. Core checks: a SIEM index nothing in the stack keeps or two declared adapters both read as theirs, a rule delivered through a SIEM with no working detection, a legal hold resting on a SIEM's retention; the log-routes report shows each environment's searchable and total days. Splunk add-on (stack role siem): indexes.conf, savedsearches.conf and Universal Forwarder inputs; reads back its confs and the REST API through a read-only collector. Microsoft Sentinel in the Azure adapter, on a Log Analytics workspace: onboarding, scheduled analytics rules, table total retention, read back. Elastic Security: its own flow.

Elastic Security as a SIEM: a siem-index destination whose reference is a logs data stream (logs-<dataset>-<namespace>) is kept by the Elastic add-on (stack role siem). Its searchable days render as an index lifecycle policy per stream (daily rollover, delete phase at the searchable days, none when kept indefinitely) attached through the dataset's @custom component template; days kept longer in all, with the archive's snapshot repository recorded, render as a daily snapshot policy expiring after the extra days, the delete phase waiting for its snapshot. Detections on a stream render as ES|QL rules counting matching events per window, every window of the rule's period breaching, with severity and risk score from the rule. Both come as Elasticsearch/Kibana API documents (the GET answer shapes, so they read back) and as Terraform for the elastic/elasticstack provider, credentials only from its environment variables. Read back from Elasticsearch (data streams with ILM or data stream lifecycle retention, snapshot archives) and Kibana (detection rules of any language), collected read-only with an API key. What it leaves to the Elastic team is named as render notes: rule actions, when a policy takes effect, archives with no place, shared datasets, Elastic Agent collection; container output is a blocker.

attributes.name: run_call
attributes.purpose: Effect: (output, problem) of one collection call: Command as a subprocess (no shell; credentials only on stdin; extra env switches; failure = 'exit N: <last 600 chars of stderr, redacted>', or not installed / timeout); a workdir Command runs in a private 0700 directory and returns {relative path: text} of what it wrote under export/ (.git never read; a symlink or non-UTF-8 file maps to None, failing the collection if kept); Request as an HTTP GET (Authorization built in memory: basic, bearer, token, headers, or api-key in the named header after an optional prefix such as Elasticsearch's 'ApiKey '; TLS trust from the CA reference or system store)

attributes.name: siem_check
attributes.purpose: The planner check for the target's SIEM indexes no adapter rendering it keeps (Adapter.siem_indexes), or more than one does (the index reads as each one's: only the first declared renders it): an action per index.

attributes.name: read_rest
attributes.purpose: Importer splunk/rest: the management API's indexes and saved searches per <cloud>/<env>/ placed into the environments (layout_import, provider None), other bindings' notices left out (siem.own_notices with naming.keeps), indexes' size limits named.

attributes.name: read_conf_files
attributes.purpose: Importer splunk/conf: indexes.conf and savedsearches.conf per <cloud>/<env>/ (the render read back, or an app's own), other bindings' notices left out (siem.own_notices with naming.keeps).

attributes.name: rest_steps
attributes.purpose: Collector steps: the two read-only GETs (indexes, saved searches) against the first location of the environment's first readable splunk/rest collection source (governance.collection.readable_source), with its credential (bearer or basic) and CA.

attributes.name: source_problems
attributes.purpose: Collector problems: why the splunk/rest collection sources can't be read (unbound credential or trust anchor, no location), from governance.collection.source_problems.

attributes.name: stream_name
attributes.purpose: The logs data stream a log destination names (its ciamProviderRef), or None when it isn't a SIEM index or its reference isn't a logs data stream name.

attributes.name: is_stream
attributes.purpose: Whether a name is a logs data stream name as Elastic names them (logs-<dataset>-<namespace>).

attributes.name: dataset_of
attributes.purpose: A data stream's type and dataset (logs-<dataset>), what its component template hook is named by.

attributes.name: custom_template
attributes.purpose: The component template a data stream's integration template composes for its dataset's own settings (<type>-<dataset>@custom).

attributes.name: policy_name
attributes.purpose: The ILM (and SLM) policy the render names after a data stream: opsdir-<stream>.

attributes.name: keeps
attributes.purpose: Adapter siem_indexes: whether log destination b of environment m is an Elastic data stream.

attributes.name: kept_streams
attributes.purpose: Environment m's Elastic data streams its render writes: those it doesn't inherit from a base environment.

attributes.name: total_days
attributes.purpose: Days a destination keeps logs in all (ciamTotalRetentionDays), or None when it records none.

attributes.name: archive_days
attributes.purpose: How many days a destination keeps its logs past its searchable days (total minus searchable; INDEFINITE when kept forever in all), or None when it keeps nothing past them.

attributes.name: snapshotted
attributes.purpose: Whether a destination's archive is rendered: it keeps logs past its searchable days and records where (ciamArchiveRef).

attributes.name: ilm_policy
attributes.purpose: (policy name, ILM policy as GET _ilm/policy answers it) of a data stream destination: hot rollover 1d/50gb, delete phase at the searchable days (wait_for_snapshot when archived; none when kept indefinitely), _meta naming the stream; None when it records no retention.

attributes.name: slm_policy
attributes.purpose: (policy name, SLM policy as GET _slm/policy answers it) archiving a data stream destination daily into its ciamArchiveRef repository, snapshots expiring after total minus searchable days; None when nothing is archived.

attributes.name: rendered_streams
attributes.purpose: Environment m's kept data streams whose policies render: each dataset's first stream recording a retention.

attributes.name: component_template
attributes.purpose: (component template name, component template as GET _component_template answers it) attaching a data stream destination's ILM policy to its dataset (index.lifecycle.name).

attributes.name: lifecycle_notes
attributes.purpose: Render notes of environment m's data streams' retention: none recorded (note), streams sharing a dataset (note when kept as long, else blocker), when each policy takes effect (action), an archive with no place recorded (action).

attributes.name: source_of
attributes.purpose: The first source an ES|QL query names (FROM <source>), or None.

attributes.name: esql_query
attributes.purpose: A detection rule's ES|QL: the detection's search counted per window (STATS COUNT BY BUCKET), each window compared with the rule's threshold, a row when every window of the period breaches.

attributes.name: base_query
attributes.purpose: A rule's own search: the one the render wrapped with an alert rule's condition, else the query as written.

attributes.name: elastic_detections
attributes.purpose: Environment m's detection AlarmSpecs on an Elastic data stream it renders (not a base environment's).

attributes.name: rule_body
attributes.purpose: The ES|QL detection rule of a detection spec as the detection engine API takes and answers it (rule_id, name, description, type/language esql, query, interval/from/to, severity and risk score, enabled, tags), or None when it isn't rendered.

attributes.name: rendered_rules
attributes.purpose: ((detection spec, rule body), ...) of environment m's detections rendered as ES|QL rules.

attributes.name: detection_notes
attributes.purpose: Render notes of environment m's Elastic detections not rendered: no search recorded (note); a condition, language or source the render can't write (blocker).

attributes.name: elastic_shipments
attributes.purpose: Environment m's Shipments whose destination is an Elastic data stream.

attributes.name: shipping_notes
attributes.purpose: Render notes of how environment m's logs reach its Elastic data streams: an action listing what Elastic Agent must collect from the servers (role, hosts, file, stream), a blocker per route whose logs are a container's output.

attributes.name: ndjson
attributes.purpose: Documents as newline-delimited JSON: one compact document per line.

attributes.name: api_files
attributes.purpose: Render target api: {elastic/api/<file>: text} of environment m's ILM policies, component templates, SLM policies (GET answer shapes) and detection rules (NDJSON for _import), each file only when it holds something.

attributes.name: lifecycle_block
attributes.purpose: The elasticstack_elasticsearch_index_lifecycle block of an ILM policy (name, GET _ilm/policy body).

attributes.name: template_block
attributes.purpose: The elasticstack_elasticsearch_component_template block of a component template (name, body).

attributes.name: snapshot_block
attributes.purpose: The elasticstack_elasticsearch_snapshot_lifecycle block of an SLM policy (name, GET _slm/policy body).

attributes.name: rule_block
attributes.purpose: The elasticstack_kibana_security_detection_rule block of a detection rule, in a Kibana space (None: the default).

attributes.name: terraform_files
attributes.purpose: Render target terraform: {elastic/terraform/versions.tf, main.tf} of environment m (elasticstack ~> 0.16.6, credentials from environment variables; notes as comments, then lifecycle, template, snapshot and rule blocks); nothing when it renders none.

attributes.name: render_notes
attributes.purpose: Adapter notes: what environment m's Elastic render leaves out or to a person (rule actions, lifecycle, detections, shipping).

attributes.name: render_env
attributes.purpose: Adapter render_env: environment m's Elastic data streams' lifecycle and detection rules in the render targets chosen (api, terraform), when it keeps logs in an Elastic data stream or runs a detection on one.

attributes.name: es_days
attributes.purpose: (whole days, None) of an Elasticsearch duration (90d, 12h, 0ms), (days rounded down, why) when it isn't whole days, or (None, why) when it isn't a duration.

attributes.name: parse_elasticsearch
attributes.purpose: (resources, notices) of one environment's Elasticsearch answers: logs data streams as siem-index destinations with searchable days (DSL data_retention or the ILM delete min_age of the stream's policy), days in all and archive repository from a covering SLM policy.

attributes.name: rule_resource
attributes.purpose: (Resource of kind alarm, notices) of one detection rule as the API gives it: the rule its description names, the stream its query searches, its search without the render's wrap, its language when not ES|QL.

attributes.name: parse_kibana
attributes.purpose: (resources, notices) of one environment's detection rules (_find pages or NDJSON), with each data stream they search as a siem-index destination alone.

attributes.name: read_elasticsearch
attributes.purpose: Importer elastic/elasticsearch: the data streams' retention per <cloud>/<env>/.

attributes.name: read_kibana
attributes.purpose: Importer elastic/kibana: the detection rules per <cloud>/<env>/ (notices about streams no rule searches left out).

attributes.name: credential
attributes.purpose: How a collection Source's credential is sent: an API key as Authorization: ApiKey <key> (api-key credential with prefix), else its scheme with its login; None when it names none.

attributes.name: elasticsearch_steps
attributes.purpose: Collector steps: GET /_data_stream, /_ilm/policy and /_slm/policy against the first readable elastic/elasticsearch source.

attributes.name: page_path
attributes.purpose: Where a page of the detection rules is saved: detection-rules.json, then detection-rules.<page>.json.

attributes.name: kibana_steps
attributes.purpose: Collector steps: the pages of _find not read yet (per_page 1000, paged by the first page's total), against the first readable elastic/kibana source, in the Kibana space the setting names.

attributes.name: problems_of
attributes.purpose: A collector's problems function for an importer: why its collection sources can't be read.

attributes.name: readable_source
attributes.parameters: [{"name": "m", "type": "EnvModel"}, {"name": "importer", "type": "str", "description": "'adapter/importer'"}, {"name": "schemes", "type": "tuple[str] | None", "required": false, "description": "credential schemes the collector accepts"}]
attributes.purpose: Environment m's first collection source for an importer that can be read: it has a location and no problems and, when schemes are given, sends its credential in one of them; None when none can (the collectors' shared idiom).

attributes.name: source_problems
attributes.purpose: Why environment m's collection sources for an importer can't be read (an unbound credential or trust anchor, no location), every source's.

attributes.name: search_language
attributes.parameters: [{"name": "b", "type": "Entry", "description": "a detection (alarm binding)"}, {"name": "native", "type": "str", "description": "the SIEM adapter's native language (spl, kusto, esql)"}]
attributes.purpose: The language a detection's search is written in (ciamSearchLanguage, attr 842), else native: the language of the SIEM keeping the index it searches.

attributes.name: own_notices
attributes.purpose: A SIEM importer's Imported without the placement's 'in the record but not in what the cloud reports' notices about entries that aren't its SIEM's: log destinations keeps(m, b) says aren't its indexes, and alarms that aren't detections searching one.

attributes.description: Item (e) of milestone 109 (analysis 3073): a new package opsdir-adapter-elastic, a third SIEM beside Splunk and Sentinel (task 530's contract: a ciamLogDestination of kind siem-index, total retention ciamRetentionDays, SIEM detections realizing the record's alert rules). Render: index lifecycle (ILM policy delete.min_age from total retention), detection engine rules for the record's detections, data streams/index templates as needed; read back: an ILM reader and detection_engine rules importer; ECS field mapping. Collector read-only against the Elasticsearch/Kibana APIs (least-privilege role, API key from a secret reference). Elastic Cloud vs self-managed and the government offering (if any) researched. Research current Elastic docs first (Codex, read-only; the Codex 6.2e report has basics); check the current Terraform provider (elastic/elasticstack) and pin its current release; design to the master before coding.
